description: The patterns that classify a meeting participant's DISPLAY NAME as a meeting-room device rather than a person. Matched case-insensitively against the display name the platform gives us. This file is the single source of truth: the TypeScript producer (bot) and the Python read path (meeting-api) each embed this table and each gate itself against this file, so the two languages cannot drift apart silently.
matching: Each `regex` is a JavaScript/Python-compatible pattern, applied case-insensitively to the trimmed display name. Any match ⇒ kind `room`.
override: Set VEXA_ROOM_PATTERNS to a JSON array of regex strings to REPLACE this table at runtime. Make the first element "+" to APPEND instead. A malformed value is ignored and these defaults stand.

patterns.why: `devices/` is Google Meet's resource-name prefix for hardware. Already treated as a non-person string by the Meet tile-name filter (core/meetings/modules/gmeet-capture/src/gmeet-speakers.ts JUNK_NAME).

The commonest shape of an admin-configured room name. Google documents that a room device's robot account carries 'the administrator-specified device name. For example, "Altostrat Room"' (Meet REST v2 conferenceRecords.participants).

`Room 2`, `Rm-14`, `Room_301` — a room identified by number. Deliberately requires the digits: the bare word `room` appears inside company and product names (a Vexa customer is literally called Roomradar), so matching it alone would misclassify people.
Calendar resources and room accounts are frequently published as `<Name> (Room)`.
Microsoft Teams Rooms devices sign in with a room resource account; Surface Hub is Microsoft's own room endpoint.
Zoom Rooms appliances join under the room's account name.
Google's own Meet hardware product names (Series One Desk 27 / Board 65; Chromebase / Chromebox for Meetings) show up verbatim in device names.
Room-system model names from the vendors that dominate Meet/Teams-certified hardware. A device left on its factory name reports the model.

The same room-word shape in the languages where our EU deployments name their rooms. Each is a compound noun that does not occur in personal names, so the false-positive risk is the same as the English `meeting room`.
